At 10.20 AM, Sensex dropped over 300 points to 74,460 while Nifty 50 lost nearly 100 points to trade below the 23,100 level. Broader markets also remained in the red, with Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 indices dropping up to 0.5%. The benchmarks Nifty and Sensex had jumped nearly 3% last week, their best weekly performances in six months, aided by a rally in IT stocks after stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings and a selloff in global AI markets that prompted value-buying elsewhere. Axis Bank shares dropped around 4% to lead losses on Sensex, while HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finserv, HUL, Infosys, NTPC, Trent and Kotak Mahindra Bank shares fell around 1% each. Bucking the trend, SBI and UltraTech Cement shares gained around 2% each, while Reliance Industries, TCS, Adani Ports, Titan, HCL Tech, L&T, Power Grid and Maruti Suzuki shares gained around 1% each. Among the sectors, Nifty PSU Bank index jumped around 3% to lead gains amid a muted market. Nifty Private Bank however slipped more than 1%. The overall market breadth turned negative, with NSE seeing 1,050 advances against 2,001 declines, while 125 stocks remained unchanged. Live Events What lies ahead for Dalal Street? By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 19, 2026, 10:02:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Jio Platforms is preparing to unveil its initial public offering, enhancing its valuation significantly. Analysts foresee a potential reduction in the holding company discount for Reliance Industries post-IPO. While some experts believe the anticipated changes are already included in the stock's valuation, the true effect on RIL shares will hinge on Jio's profitability and future dividend plans. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-135039750,width-210,height-158,imgsize-2264128,resizemode-75/holding-company-discount-after-jio-ipo-what-is-it-amp-how-will-it-impact-ril-sharesbr.jpg"> ETMarkets.com Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries could see part of its longstanding holding company discount shrink when Jio Platforms lists on the stock exchanges later this month. But analysts are divided over how much of that benefit will translate into gains for RIL shareholders, with some arguing that the much-awaited listing has already been factored into the stock's valuation. The debate comes as Jio Platforms prepares to launch its Rs 30,213 crore initial public offering on October 21, valuing the telecom and digital services company at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore at the upper end of its price band. For Reliance Industries, which currently owns about 66.4% of Jio Platforms, that valuation puts its stake at roughly Rs 6.8 lakh crore. The question is whether the stock market is assigning the parent company the full value of that holding. What is holding company discount? A holding company discount arises when a parent company's stock market valuation is lower than the combined estimated value of the businesses and investments it owns, after accounting for debt and other liabilities. Investors often apply such discounts because shareholders of the parent do not directly own or control its subsidiaries' assets. The discount can also reflect corporate complexity, taxes associated with selling investments, capital allocation concerns and uncertainty over when the value of subsidiaries will reach shareholders. Live Events In Reliance's case, investors are valuing a diversified group with interests spanning oil refining, petrochemicals, telecom, retail and new energy. Even if Jio commands a higher valuation after listing, that does not automatically mean RIL shares will rise by a corresponding amount. Prathamesh Kadival, Research Analyst at Bonanza, estimates that RIL shares currently reflect a 36% discount on its stake in Jio, compared with a more reasonable discount of around 25% after listing. At Jio's proposed valuation, an 11-percentage-point narrowing would represent approximately Rs 75,000 crore in additional implied value for RIL's stake, assuming the discount is applied directly to that holding. By Debaroti Adhikary , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 19, 2026, 09:58:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Yes Bank shares rose after falling 17% over two sessions, following a 65% year-on-year jump in Q2 net profit to Rs 1,080 crore. However, the lender cautioned that the reported earnings exclude the potential impact of the Supreme Court’s AT1 bond ruling. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-135039646,width-210,height-158,imgsize-214694,resizemode-75/yes-bank-shares-rise-as-q2-profit-beats-estimates-but-at1-bond-verdict-hit-pegged-at-rs-5217-crore-what-lies-aheadbr.jpg"> ETMarkets.com A legal setback over AT1 bonds has put Yes Bank’s reported quarterly profit under scrutiny. Yes Bank shares gained a little more than 1% on Monday, following a 17% plunge over the past two sessions, as the private lender reported a 65% year-on-year increase in Q2 net profit to Rs 1,080 crore. The lender, however, said the figure does not reflect the impact of a Supreme Court ruling that set aside the bank's 2020 write-off of Rs 8,400 crore worth of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds. The Mumbai-based lender would have reported a quarterly loss of Rs 5,217 crore if the impact of the Supreme Court’s ruling was recognised in the earnings print, the bank said in a regulatory filing. This came after the Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a 2023 Bombay High Court judgment that set aside the write-off, dismissing appeals filed by Yes Bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the central government, triggering a sharp selloff in the stock. The bank said the reported figures were indicative and subject to revision as it assessed the implications of the ruling. Also read | YES Bank Q2 profit rises 65%; AT1 hit may risk 5,217 cr loss Yes Bank’s net interest income (NII), which represents the difference between interest earned on loans and interest paid on deposits, rose 22.7% year on year to Rs 2,822 crore. Advances grew 23.7% from a year earlier, while deposits increased 19.5%. Provisions for bad loans and other contingencies fell 24.2% to Rs 317 crore. Other income rose 14.4% to Rs 1,882 crore. The private lender’s asset quality also improved during the quarter. The gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio stood at 1.2% at the end of September, compared with 1.3% at the end of June. Live Events Yes Bank’s earnings announcement on Saturday came after the AT1 ruling. The dispute dates back to March 2020, when Yes Bank was placed under a moratorium by the RBI following a sharp deterioration in its financial position, mounting bad loans and concerns over governance. The central bank subsequently introduced a reconstruction scheme, under which State Bank of India and several other lenders invested capital to rescue the struggling bank.

Shares of HDFC Bank, India’s largest private lender, slipped as much as 2% to Rs 715 on the BSE on Monday after it reported a net profit of Rs 19,510 crore for the second quarter of FY27, marking a 4.6% jump from Rs 18,641 crore posted in the same period last year. HDFC Bank’s net interest income (interest earned less interest expended) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, rose 9.7% to Rs 34,620 crore from Rs 31,550 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Net interest margin stood at 3.16% on total assets and 3.32% on interest-earning assets. What should HDFC Bank shareholders do? Jefferies has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on HDFC Bank with a target price of Rs 880, implying an upside of 21%. The brokerage said the bank’s credit quality remained robust, with gross slippages at 0.9% of loans from the past year, compared with 1.2% a year earlier. Jefferies has factored in some increase in credit costs for FY28-29 to reflect a normalisation in credit experience and the transition to expected credit loss (ECL) norms. The brokerage has also revised its FY27-29 estimates to account for rate hikes and FCNR-B deposits. HDFC Bank's new CEO is set to take charge on October 27, while deputy managing director Kaizad has submitted his resignation, seeking to be relieved from December 31, 2026. Jefferies said clarity on new appointments and changes to the senior management team will be key to watch. The brokerage considers the bank's valuations reasonable at 1.4 times FY28 estimated adjusted price-to-book value and 11 times price-to-earnings. It also expects profit before tax, excluding treasury operations, to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 13% over FY26-29. Live Events Motilal Oswal has maintained its positive view on HDFC Bank, with a target price of Rs 925, implying an upside of 27%. The brokerage said the bank delivered a largely in-line quarter, supported by healthy business growth and strong operating profit, although provisions remained elevated.
